sections.text: ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः।
He who dedicates his actions to the Spirit, without any personal attachment to them, he is no more tainted by sin than the water lily is wetted by water.
The sage performs his action dispassionately, using his body, mind and intellect, and even his senses, always as a means of purification.

Having abandoned the fruit of action, he wins eternal peace. Others unacquainted with spirituality, led by desire and clinging to the benefit which they think will follow their actions, become entangled in them.

We had been discussing chapter five, Karma Sannyasa Yoga, Yoga of Renunciation of Actions. So far we have learnt in Bhagavad Gita that the self which I consider myself is not the real self. We learnt in chapter two, Sankhya Yoga. So the entire quest in our life is to reconcile this paradox we have. We consider ourselves to be a limited being. But Bhagavad Gita says, you are not the limited being.
So how do I remove this paradox? How do I change this paradigm with which Im functioning right now as an individual limited being, and identify with that unlimited supreme being? Thats basically the goal of the rest of the teachings of Bhagavad Gita. So in chapter three, Bhagavan said, you can start with Karma Yoga, Yoga of Action. Act you must, but act in a way that does not bind you, so that you can free yourself from this conditioning. You act in this world without an expectation for the fruits, because you are not in control of the fruits.
Right now I consider myself to be completely separate from this world, and Im competing with this world. Bhagavan said, unless you give up this identity of your own, you will not be able to realize your true identity. The Upanishads tell us that the world which I see is finite, but that supreme is unlimited, infinite, Almighty, all-knowing. But for me to perceive that is very, very difficult. So therefore we chant this: Om Purnamadhah Purnamidam Purnath Purnamuddhachate Purnasya Purnamadaya Purnamavashate. It says that from that infinite came this infinite which I see as infinite.
Jagat, this Prakriti, is also complete and infinite. That from which it came, the supreme Brahman, is also infinite. That is infinite. This is also infinite. The world Im identifying with is also infinite, even though it seems finite. Even though I see myself as a finite being in a world that appears finite -- its not finite, its infinite. And if you take this infinite out of that infinite, what remains is still infinite.
In other words, there is no separation between the world which I perceive and the real self. There is no separation between my limited self and that supreme self. But ignorance is creating this dual vision, and I need to remove that. So the first step is: when you act in this world, see this unity and dont expect any results from your actions. That will relieve you from the anxiety of the fruits of actions. And then chapter four said there are not really two separate entities. Both came from the same singular entity, and therefore act for the betterment of the entire Jagat.
The Jagat that you consider your own world -- maybe your own family, maybe your own community, maybe your own nation. Work for that without expecting that your actions will bear particular results; that will free you from anxiety. And now in this chapter, we are learning how to renounce this sense of agency -- that I am the doer.
So Bhagavan started this chapter saying you can reach that same goal by renouncing actions and also by performing actions. Renouncing actions in the knowledge that I am not the doer will take you to that place where you can identify with your supreme self. But performing actions in this world without any expectations will also lead you to that state, by purifying your internal instrument, which right now is conditioned by this limitedness that you have taken upon yourself as your own.
Bhagavan said both are one and the same. Yatsangkhi prapyate sthanam tadyogi apigema. That place which is reached by contemplation on the very fact we learnt in chapter two -- that I am not this mortal being, I am that immortal being. If I contemplate on that statement and come to the conclusion that thats the truth, I change my identification from this limited self to the higher self. Thats the path of Sankhya -- contemplating on that great statement Tattvamasi, you are that. But if thats not in my capability right now, Bhagavan said, tat yoge API gammade.
By performing this Karma Yoga, you can also achieve that same state, the same result. And therefore you should start with Karma Yoga. Because contemplation without preparing your mind for the contemplation is pretty painful. In other words, it will not bear any good result. And then you will be frustrated. And then you will say, I dont think this has any value.
So rather than engaging yourself in Something youre not capable of, engage yourself in purifying your mind and intellect. The yogi who has achieved the state of purification, he knows that naiva kinchit karomi ITI yuktaham manyate tattvavit. One who knows the essence of the self, that that which feels like my limited self is nothing but the supreme self. It is my own ignorance that Im identifying with the limitations and therefore I feel limited. One who has recognized that truth by establishing himself in yoga or by contemplation, he knows that naivakinchitkarami I am not doing anything. Everything is performed by indriyani indriyarthesu vartanta ITI dharayan.
He clearly sees that what I perceive as activity performed by me is nothing but senses reacting with sense objects. And we can clearly see through our normal observations that my sense of taste will indulge me into eating more sweets, and that will show up on my body. So it is the sense objects and senses reacting with each other. Or I may consider myself to be a very wise person with control over my intellect and mind, but just one substance from this world called alcohol -- if I indulge in it, all my wisdom and sanity will go away and I will act like an average idiot.
So we know that these sense objects have clear effect on my behavior, a clear effect on how I think. And therefore I have to come to the conclusion that indriyaani indriya teshu vartnantah, the senses are indulging in activity with the sense objects. So all the activities, all that which is good and how that is bad is nothing but purely the interaction between the senses and sense objects. And we have seen sabdas parsa rupa rasa gandha, the five sense objects, and kshutra thvaka chakshuhu rasana grana, the five senses we have, you remove one, then the world of that sense will go away. If you remove all five, the world of objects which I perceive will go away. So therefore Bhagavan says, Brahmani adhaya karmani sangam tyaktva karotiyah.
So now, I am not at the level of that Yogi who clearly sees naiva kinchit karomi -- I am not doing anything. He does not have this confusion that I have. I think I am doing this, I have done this, I have not done this -- he does not have that confusion. He is like the ocean which sees its own waves and sees that he, as the ocean, is not involved in the activities of the waves. The waves are the water reacting with the wind, creating these waves on the surface.
But at the bottom, the ocean is standing still. They say Brahmani Adhaya Karmani Sangam Tyaktva Karutiyah. The phrase Sangam Tyaktva comes, as Sid pointed out last time, in this verse, and then Karma Phalam Tyaktva in the third verse. This word Tyaktva is constantly coming in our discussion. Anytime we see the word Tyaktva, it clearly means we are already attached. It means give up, abandon.
I can only do that if I have something which I have to give up. So this clearly says that Sangam Tyaktva I am already attached. Its given that Im attached to this world. Im attached to this body, Im attached to this mind, Im attached to my intellect. No matter how hard I try, I keep identifying with who I am. As this limited being.
The idea that I am the doer does not go away very easily. Therefore, Bhagavan said, there is a method to get rid of that. Your mind has a tendency to attach, and if you dont give it an alternate, you will never be able to give up your attachment. So the alternate: Brahmani Yadhaya Karmani -- you offer all your actions to that supreme. That supreme which is complete. There is no place for you to be there as an individual.
If that supreme is all-pervading, all-complete -- if Im all-pervading in my chair, theres no place for somebody else to be here. If that supreme is all-pervading, there is no place for me as a little ego to be there. And therefore, offer all your actions to that supreme. Brahmani Yadhaya Karmani, Sangam Tyaktva -- first you have to detach yourself from this attachment.
So by attaching yourself to Brahman, you offer all actions to him. Right now Im bound by all my actions. I get success and I get elated. I get failure and I get dejected. When I get dejected and disappointed, it creates a negative impression in my mind -- that is the sin Im incurring. So now the exercise for you, Bhagavan said, is this: because you are not at that level of a Yogi, you offer all your actions to him. Continue working, but think that you are not working for yourself -- you are working for him.
Whatever the results come, that will be his loss or profit, not yours. This analogy comes in our scriptures all the time. Just as lotus leaf is in the water, but does not get moistened by the water, it comes out of water, goes back into the water, decays in water, but during its lifetime it never gets moistened by the water. The same way you came in this world, you live in this world. You will die in this world. But while living, you dont get attached to the world by attaching yourself to Brahman.
So here is the technique Bhagavan has given for giving up the sense of agency, for those of us who are still at a level where we think that we are the doers. Kayana, Manasa, Buddhaya, Kaivalay, Indriyahiyapi, Yogi nahakarma, Karvanti, Sangam tyaktva atma sudaye. Again the words Sangam Tyaktva -- by giving up attachment, because right now I am attached. That fact has to be acknowledged first, and then we can say what is my next step. It is like Alcoholics Anonymous.
The first step is to admit that Im an alcoholic. See, the first step is to admit that I am attached to this world -- to my body, my mind, my intellect, and my senses. Therefore, now I should recognize that I am not the one instigating all these activities. The activities are done by my body, because the very nature of the body is to function. Manasa -- by my mind, because the very nature of mind is to go out and get attached. Buddha -- my intellect, because the very nature of my intellect is to think what is right, what is wrong, what I have experienced, what I have not experienced. And my senses -- the very nature of the senses is to go out and get impressions from the world outside. Those impressions, now reported to the mind, create impressions on the mind.
Those impressions on the mind create perceptions in my intellect, and then I become the doer of the activity. But once I detach myself from all of this -- Kaya, Mana, Buddhi, and Indriya -- they are independent of me. They are acting according to their own nature. But I, the consciousness, the self, am not involved in it. Yogi Naha, Karma, Kurvanti, Sangam tyaktva atma sudaye.
So here clearly Bhagavan gives us the goal. The goal is the purification of the internal instrument Atma.

The lotus leaf analogy in verse 10 offers a powerful image for daily life: living in the world without being stained by it, just as the lotus remains in water yet never gets wet. Verse 11 reveals the purpose of this detached engagement - atmasuddhaye, for the purification of the self. This is not passive withdrawal but active purification. Verse 12 then presents the clear choice: one who abandons the fruit of action wins eternal peace, while one driven by desire becomes entangled.
Today, offer your actions to the Spirit as verse 10 instructs. Before beginning any task, silently acknowledge: This action is offered to the Divine. The results belong to the Divine. Notice how this shifts your relationship with the work. The recurring phrase sangam tyaktva (giving up attachment) appears twice in these verses - acknowledge that you are currently attached, and that is precisely why this practice is necessary. Like Alcoholics Anonymous begins with admitting the problem, spiritual growth begins with acknowledging our attachments. Track your inner state during one significant activity today: Are you performing it for purification (atmasuddhaye) or for personal gain? The quality of your inner peace will reveal the answer. Can you be like the lotus - fully present in your environment yet untouched by its turbulence?
